text:
sophia: Heads-up — since the fw tighten at 04:00 UTC ~30% of ap-south GPU nodes are failing to finish provisioning. Symptoms: node bootstrap stuck, container failed to contact HSM proxy, and audit writes to central bucket time out.

kevin: linking logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/ap-south/provision/1719819 — looks like TCP timeouts to 10.20.5.0/24 and repeated kms:Decrypt AccessDenied for node role. ops-oncall, can you confirm?

ops-oncall: investigating. grabbing node bootstrap.log from a failing instance. snippets: 
```
2026-03-20T04:08:12Z ERROR hsm-proxy: connect timeout to 10.20.5.11:443
2026-03-20T04:08:16Z WARN iam: Sts assume-role failed: AccessDenied
2026-03-20T04:09:02Z ERROR audit: failed to PUT s3://central-audit/ap-south/2026-03-20.json 403
```
Looks like egress to HSM proxy + S3 writes are blocked.

irene: this came from the egress rule change that went in during the maintenance window. The intent was to restrict unknown outbound addresses but we only whitelisted public KMS endpoints and the S3 VPC endpoint — forgot the internal HSM proxy CIDR and ephemeral NAT ports.

thomas: quick mitigation plan: 1) reopen egress to 10.20.5.0/24 (HSM proxy) for the GPU subnets, 2) allow outbound ephemeral ports 1024-65535 to NAT for TLS handshakes, 3) grant a short-lived audit role so nodes can finish writes. Do we have approval to do a one-hour exception?

sophia: yes, we need the fleet healthy asap. the business impact: customer latency spikes and queued jobs piling up. cost note: autoscaler is keeping instances running waiting for bootstrap, so this is already ~+$3k/hr while we have stuck nodes.

kevin: infra prefers to push terraform change rather than manual iptables. ops-oncall, can you apply a scoped iptables patch to unblock bootstraps while infra prepares TF? keep it ephemeral (10m ttl).

ops-oncall: applied iptables patch to ap-south-gpu-subnet-a with TTL=10m. command used: 
```
# on bastion
sudo iptables -I OUTPUT -d 10.20.5.0/24 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 1024:65535 -j ACCEPT
# schedule removal in 600s
```
Nodes started draining bootstrap logs showing successful HSM handshake.

irene: preparing TF change now. terraform snippet: 
```
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "egress_hsm_ap_south" {
  type              = "egress"
  from_port         = 443
  to_port           = 443
  protocol          = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks       = ["10.20.5.0/24"]
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.gpu_nodes.id
  description       = "allow hsm proxy egress for gpu bootstrap"
}
```
Will run `terraform apply` on the infra PR once compliance signoff is captured.

kevin: also need IAM temporary workaround for audit writer. ops-oncall can you run: 
```
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/audit-writer --role-session-name gpu-bootstrap-ephemeral --duration-seconds 3600
```
and export creds on the failing node agent? Keep the scope minimal.

ops-oncall: done. I assumed audit-writer for 1h and pushed creds to the node agent on 3 affected instances. audit writes resumed.

deploy-bot: deploy 1719820000: terraform plan for egress rule created by irene in PR #4921. CI green.

compliance-bot: Requesting justification and risk assessment for temporary egress exception (10.20.5.0/24) and 1h audit-role assumption. Please provide: business impact, data sensitivity, retention implications. Tagging @compliance for signoff.

sophia: justification: major customer-facing workload stuck, multi-hour job queues, cost bleed (~$3k/hr). Data path: only node bootstrap and audit writes to central bucket; retention unchanged. We will remove the temporary iptables rule and revoke assumed role creds after TF applied.

irene: PR #4921 approved by infra leads, scheduling `terraform apply` in 2m. Will include explicit SG description and TTL annotation for audit trace.

kevin: after apply, we should run quick smoke: 
```
kubectl -n infra rollout status daemonset/gpu-bootstrap -w
curl -sS https://logs.redwood.internal/ap-south/provision/health | grep HSM
```
Confirming nodes are healthy now.

ops-oncall: smoke passed for 12/12 nodes in subnet-a, 8/8 in subnet-b still warming. Rolling capacity back to normal.

compliance-bot: signoff recorded: temporary exception logged with justification and will be auto-revoked at 05:30 UTC. Please attach PR link and removal ticket.

sophia: thanks all — follow-up: create a test in our e2e infra suite to simulate blocked HSM egress so we catch this in staging next time.

thomas: noted, will add a terraform guard and an automated verification for HSM proxy connectivity during rollout. :thumbsup:

kevin: marking thread resolved once PR lands and ttl rules removed.
